models.name: IPA
models.subtitle: Compact Inception network
models.description: A compact convolutional network with parallel Inception branches with different kernel sizes.
models.citation: Haffner et al. (2025), IPA: A deep CNN based on Inception for Petroleum Analysis, Fuel 379, 133016.

models.name: 1D-CNN · 1L–3
models.subtitle: One wide convolution
models.description: One convolutional filter with a 31-channel kernel, followed by a 128 → 64 → 16 dense head.
models.citation: CNN baseline architecture; Used in different papers.

models.name: 1D-CNN · 1N–3
models.subtitle: One narrow convolution
models.description: One convolutional filter with a 5-channel kernel and the same dense head as the wide-kernel baseline.
models.citation: CNN baseline architecture; Used in different papers.

models.name: 1D-CNN · 3–1
models.subtitle: Three convolutional blocks
models.description: A sequential baseline with 16, 32 and 64 filters, pooling, global average pooling and a dense regression head.
models.citation: CNN baseline architecture; Used in different papers

models.name: DeepSpectra
models.subtitle: Multiple spectral scales
models.description: An Inception-style 1D CNN that combines convolutional kernels at several scales, with dropout and L2 regularization.
models.citation: Zhang et al. (2019), DeepSpectra: An end-to-end deep learning approach for quantitative spectral analysis, Analytica Chimica Acta 1058, 48–57.

models.name: 1D Inception-ResNet
models.subtitle: Inception meets residual learning
models.description: A deeper convolutional architecture combining parallel Inception branches with residual connections.
models.citation: Tan et al. (2023), 1D-inception-resnet for NIR quantitative analysis and its transferability between different spectrometers, Infrared Physics & Technology 129, 104559.

models.name: ResidualSpectra
models.subtitle: Residual spectral features
models.description: A residual convolutional network adapted to continuous, single-target prediction from spectra.
models.citation: Wang et al. (2020), End-to-end analysis modeling of vibrational spectroscopy based on deep learning approach, Journal of Chemometrics, e3291.

models.name: SpectraNet32
models.subtitle: Residual CNN
models.description: A residual spectral network adapted to single-output regression, with parametric GELU, dropout and regularization.
models.citation: Martins et al. (2023), Estimation of soluble solids content and fruit temperature in ‘Rocha’ pear using Vis-NIR spectroscopy and the SpectraNet–32 deep learning architecture, Postharvest Biology and Technology 199, 112281.

models.name: SpectraNet53
models.subtitle: Deep spectral CNN
models.description: A deeper spectral CNN with PReLU/GELU activations, dropout, L2 regularization and gradient clipping.
models.citation: Martins et al. (2022), SpectraNet–53: A deep residual learning architecture for predicting soluble solids content with VIS–NIR spectroscopy, Computers and Electronics in Agriculture 197, 106945.

models.name: MarkSpectra
models.subtitle: Select spectral marks
models.description: The benchmark implementation selects informative wavelength marks and fits a compact dense regression network.
models.citation: Wang et al. (2022), Mark-Spectra: A convolutional neural network for quantitative spectral analysis overcoming spatial relationships, Computers and Electronics in Agriculture 192, 106624.

models.name: SCNet
models.subtitle: Multiscale shortcut CNN
models.description: A multiscale convolutional network that pools and concatenates features from successive convolution stages before the dense regression head.
models.citation: Li et al. (2023), SCNet: A deep learning network framework for analyzing near-infrared spectroscopy using short-cut, Infrared Physics & Technology 132, 104731.

models.name: Spectraformer
models.subtitle: Convolutions + attention
models.description: Convolutional feature extraction combined with Transformer blocks for spectral regression.
models.citation: Chen, Zhou & Ren (2024), Spectraformer: deep learning model for grain spectral qualitative analysis based on transformer structure, RSC Advances 14, 8053–8066.

models.name: SpectraTr
models.subtitle: Spectra as patches
models.description: A vision-Transformer-style architecture with patching adjusted to each dataset’s spectral length.
models.citation: Fu et al. (2022), SpectraTr: A novel deep learning model for qualitative analysis of drug spectroscopy based on transformer structure, Journal of Innovative Optical Health Sciences 15, 2250021.

models.name: TabPFN-3.5
models.subtitle: Pretrained tabular regressor
models.description: Frozen pretrained weights use the full training set as context. Ten seeds vary its internal ensemble; no epoch selection or CV is performed. Free model available from PriorLabs.
models.citation: Hollmann et al. (2025), Accurate predictions on small data with a tabular foundation model, Nature 637, 319–326.

models.name: PLS regression
models.subtitle: The optimized chemometric reference
models.description: Five-fold training-set CV jointly selects one of nine spectral preprocessings and 1–20 latent variables before a final fit on the full training split. Using Scikit-Learn implementation.
models.citation: Wold, Sjöström & Eriksson (2001), PLS-regression: a basic tool of chemometrics, Chemometrics and Intelligent Laboratory Systems 58, 109–130.

provenance.population: 30 task configurations. Mango tasks 22–25 use seed-42 80/20 splits of inferred fruit groups (equal DM within each season). Some tasks share samples, targets or instruments.
provenance.uncertainty: Sample standard deviation across final seeded runs, not a confidence interval. PLS is one fit.
provenance.ranking: Mean of 100 × (M − rank)/(M − 1), with average ties, on shared datasets only.
provenance.time: Comparative wall time measured on a common Windows 11 workstation (Intel Core i9-13900K and NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti, WSL2, TensorFlow 2.20). DL records each final fit plus train/test prediction; TabPFN-3.5 records fit plus test prediction; PLS records its five-fold joint preprocessing and latent-variable optimization.
